name: Bitcoin
h1: Casinos that accept Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals
metaTitle: Bitcoin Casinos: Deposit and Payout Reality Check
metaDescription: Casinos accepting Bitcoin for both deposits and withdrawals, with the fee and confirmation-time trade-offs that decide whether BTC is the right coin to play in.
intro:
Bitcoin support is close to universal among the casinos we track, so the useful question is not whether a site accepts it but whether BTC is the coin you should actually be using there.

On the deposit side it rarely matters. You send, it confirms, you play, and most operators credit after one confirmation. The friction shows up on the way out.

An on-chain Bitcoin withdrawal carries a network fee that someone has to pay, and the answer differs by operator: some absorb it, some deduct it from the payout, and a few apply a flat charge that bears no relationship to actual network conditions. During congestion the difference between a site that pays the fee and one that passes it on can be several dollars on a small cashout. That is worth checking in the terms before you deposit, because it is almost never mentioned on the page advertising the bonus.

Confirmation time is the other half. On-chain BTC is the slowest of the common options, and a payout the casino released in seconds can still take twenty minutes or more to appear. A minority of operators support Lightning, which sidesteps this entirely — the same withdrawal settles in under a second for a negligible fee — and Lightning support is a genuine differentiator worth filtering for if you cash out often in small amounts.

Where Bitcoin does win is availability and liquidity. It is the coin every operator supports, the one every exchange lists, and the one least likely to be quietly dropped from a payments page. If you play across several sites, holding a balance in BTC means never discovering that the casino you wanted to try does not take your coin. If you play at one site and withdraw weekly, a stablecoin on a cheap chain will almost always cost you less.

The minimum deposit is the last thing to check. It is usually denominated in BTC rather than dollars, which means a threshold set during a different market makes for an uncomfortable surprise; the figures on each casino page are current as of our last verification pass.

faq.q: Do Bitcoin casinos charge a withdrawal fee?
faq.a: It varies. Some absorb the network fee, some deduct it from the payout, and some apply a flat charge unrelated to actual network conditions. It is stated in the terms rather than on the promotional pages.

faq.q: How long does a Bitcoin withdrawal take?
faq.a: The casino's own release can be instant, but on-chain confirmation typically adds ten to thirty minutes and longer when the network is busy. Lightning withdrawals, where offered, settle in about a second.
